subject: FintechCo - Post-demo performance & SLO checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Park <john.park@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: FintechCo - Post-demo performance & SLO checklist

Hi John / Sarah -

Thanks again for the time today. Per our demo, I wanted to capture the perf/SLO details we discussed and outline the immediate next steps (MAP) so your team can evaluate Redwood against the decision criteria you shared.

High-level summary (from demo):
- Use case: real-time transaction classification and fraud detection for UX flows (avg request ~ 120 tokens, some up to 600 tokens).
- Expected steady-state: ~20k queries/day (avg), peak concurrency ~200-250 concurrent active users, burst to ~600 concurrent for 10-15s events.

SLO / perf targets you mentioned:
- P95 latency (end-to-end, server-side): <= 350 ms for synchronous responses for payloads <= 512 tokens.
- Streaming (token-by-token): first-byte latency <= 120 ms; sustained per-token latency <= 30 ms for subsequent tokens.
- Throughput: sustained ~50k tokens/minute; bursting to ~250k tokens/min for short windows.
- Concurrency: support 200 steady concurrent streams with graceful degradation and prioritization for high-value requests.
- Availability: 99.9% SLA for the dedicated offering (discussed as requirement).

Notes / clarifications:
- The p95 above is measured at the Redwood service edge (we typically report server-side end-to-end excluding the customer network hop). We can also provide browser-to-server measurements if you want end-to-end numbers.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching is available and will materially reduce token cost and p95 for repeat queries; cold-cache datapoints will be different and we'll include both in the benchmark report.

Attached: initial SLO checklist (fintechco_slo_checklist.xlsx) and demo recording link.

Proposed MAP (short-term):
1) FintechCo provides a representative sample workload (CSV or load script + 1k representative prompts) - owner: FintechCo (John) - due: 2027-03-16
2) Redwood runs a hosted benchmark against the workload (warm and cold cache) and provides a p50/p95/p99 breakdown + token cost estimates - owner: Marissa/Rishi - due: 2027-03-19
3) Quick follow-up call to review results and decide POC configuration (hosted vs dedicated + quantization profile) - owner: Marissa/John - target: 2027-03-22
4) Procurement/pricing discussion (if POC accepted) - owner: Procurement teams - target: 2027-03-26

Decision criteria checklist (what you said matters most):
- Meets p95 latency target under expected concurrency (must)
- Predictable burst behavior and graceful fallback (must)
- Cost per 1k tokens within expected budget (should)
- Security controls: SOC2, VPC & KMS (must for production)

Quick asks from our side:
- Can you confirm the sample workload format you prefer (CSV of prompts vs replay script)?
- Any hard constraints on cold-cache vs warm-cache expectations?

Happy to sync up tomorrow if you'd like - otherwise we'll wait for the sample workload and run the bench.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: fintechco_slo_checklist.xlsx

From: John Park <john.park@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: FintechCo - Post-demo performance & SLO checklist

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. A few quick questions before we assemble the workload: 

1) When you say p95 is measured at the service edge, does that exclude TLS handshake time and our internal network latency? We care about end-user experience, so an estimate that includes the client-to-edge hop would be helpful.

2) For streaming, can you confirm you support chunked token streaming in browsers (SSE / chunked HTTP) and whether first-byte numbers are typically stable across regions?

3) Warm vs cold cache: for our use case the majority of user flows reuse cached prefixes, but we expect some cold-cache bursts (e.g., new users). Would you include a 15% cold-cache scenario in the benchmark?

We'd like Redwood to run both server-edge numbers and a synthetic browser-to-edge run (we can simulate with a few NAT'd clients). Also please include a note on how you throttle or prioritize during bursts - we need to ensure fraud decisions are prioritized over low-value requests.

Finally, procurement asked about estimated pricing for a pilot (1 month, expected token volume ~1.2M tokens) and whether a short Dedicated trial is possible. Can you loop in pricing/contact who can issue a quote?

I'll assemble the CSV of prompts unless you'd prefer a replay script. Thanks - I'll target sending the sample by Tue 2027-03-16.

Best,
John Park
Product Lead, Risk & Fraud | FintechCo
john.park@fintechco.com | +1 (212) 555-0147

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Park <john.park@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, procurement@fintechco.com
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 14:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: FintechCo - Post-demo performance & SLO checklist

Thanks John - answers inline below + updated MAP and tech notes.

1) p95 measurement: the standard report we provide is server-edge (post-TLS terminate) which excludes the customer last-mile. We can run an additional browser-to-edge synthetic (SSE or chunked HTTP) to give you end-to-end approximations; that will add ~20-60 ms depending on region and network path. We'll include both in the deliverable.

2) Streaming: yes - we support chunked token streaming for browsers (HTTP/1.1 chunked and HTTP/2/3 push-friendly streaming). First-byte stability across regions varies with network hop; inside the same cloud region it's consistent within ~20 ms, cross-region adds variability. We'll run the streaming test from us-east-1 to mirror your primary traffic.

3) Cold-cache: we'll include three runs in the benchmark - cold-cache baseline, warm-cache steady-state, and a mixed scenario (15% cold traffic) as you requested.

Burst handling / prioritization: Redwood supports request-priority policies at the routing layer. For the bench we'll configure high-priority lanes for fraud decision endpoints (isolated queues + token limits) so your high-value flows are protected in bursts. We'll document the QoS behavior and the fallback model (model variant downgrade or reduced max concurrency).

Pricing / Dedicated trial: I'll loop in our pricing lead (cc'ed: Stephanie) - Stephanie can follow up with a pilot quote for 1 month (1.2M tokens) and options for a short Dedicated trial (14-day reserved capacity eval).

Updated MAP (owners/dates):
- John: provide sample workload (CSV) and preferred test format - due 2027-03-16
- Marissa/Rishi: run hosted benchmarks (cold/warm/mixed + streaming) and produce report incl. p50/p95/p99, token cost estimates, QoS behavior - due 2027-03-19
- Marissa/John: review results in follow-up call - propose 2027-03-22 (30m)
- Stephanie/FintechCo procurement: pilot quote & Dedicated trial options - due 2027-03-18

Deliverables we'll provide: benchmark report (CSV + PDF), replay logs, recommended config (batching, quantization profile), and a short runbook for prioritization and autoscale knobs.

Next practical step: John - if you send the CSV (or a replay script) I'll confirm receipt and kick off the bench.

Thanks,
Marissa
